title: Grammar: Quantifiers — All, Every, Each, Both, Neither, Either
grammarTip:
Квантификаторы — сколько? сколько много?

ALL / MOST / SOME / ANY / NO:
All students passed. · Most students passed. · Some failed. · None failed.

MUCH / MANY / A LOT OF / LOTS OF:
Much + неисчисляемые: much time · much money · much information
Many + исчисляемые: many students · many books · many hours
A lot of / lots of + оба типа (в разговорной речи)

A LITTLE / A FEW / LITTLE / FEW:
a little = немного (достаточно): "I have a little time."
little = почти нет (мало): "I have little time." (проблема!)
a few = несколько (достаточно): "I have a few friends."
few = почти нет: "Few people know this." (редкость)

💡 Разница a little/few vs little/few = оптимизм vs пессимизм!

grammarExtra.title: All vs Every vs Each: Key Differences

rows.form: ALL: group together, with plural verb
rows.example: "All patients need support." "All of the results were positive."

rows.form: EVERY: one by one, with singular verb — emphasises individual members
rows.example: "Every patient needs individual attention." "Every single result was checked."

rows.form: EACH: individual members, often in smaller groups or in sequence
rows.example: "Each patient was given a different treatment." "She spoke to each person in the group."

rows.form: EVERY/EACH cannot be used with two things
rows.example: "Both (not every/each) of the two options are valid."

grammarExtra.title: Both, Either, Neither: For Exactly Two

rows.form: BOTH: two things/people together (positive)
rows.example: "Both the doctor and the patient agreed." "Both treatments are effective."

rows.form: EITHER: one or the other (positive choice or negative with not)
rows.example: "You can take either tablet." "She didn't respond to either treatment."

rows.form: NEITHER: not one AND not the other (negative meaning)
rows.example: "Neither medication worked." "Neither of the patients improved."

rows.form: Neither/either + singular verb (unless "of" construction)
rows.example: "Neither doctor is available." BUT "Neither of the doctors are/is available." (both OK)

grammarExtra.title: All of / Both of / Neither of / Each of + the/pronoun

rows.form: all of + the + noun / pronoun
rows.example: "All of the patients recovered." "All of them were discharged."

rows.form: both of + the + noun / pronoun
rows.example: "Both of the studies showed the same result." "Both of them agreed."

rows.form: neither of + the + noun / pronoun (+ singular or plural verb)
rows.example: "Neither of the treatments worked." / "Neither of them were available."

rows.form: each of + the + noun / pronoun (+ singular verb)
rows.example: "Each of the patients received a different dose." "Each of them was examined."

grammarExtra.title: Whole vs All: Difference in Meaning

rows.form: whole = complete / uninterrupted
rows.example: "She slept for the whole night." (= without waking up)

rows.form: all = every part of / total amount
rows.example: "She slept all night." (= throughout the night)

rows.form: the whole + singular noun (not plural)
rows.example: "The whole country was affected." (not "the whole countries")

rows.form: all + plural noun (general)
rows.example: "All countries were affected." (general — no "the")

grammarExtra.title: Common Errors with All, Every, Both, Neither

rows.form: ❌ Every patients received treatment.
rows.example: ✅ Every patient received treatment. (every + singular noun)

rows.form: ❌ Neither of the options are available. (strict grammar)
rows.example: ✅ Neither of the options is available. (singular after "neither of" in formal English)

rows.form: ❌ Both of them is correct.
rows.example: ✅ Both of them are correct. (both = plural → plural verb)

rows.form: ❌ I didn't take neither of them.
rows.example: ✅ I took neither of them. / I didn't take either of them. (no double negative)

exercises.text: "___ patient in the ward received the new medication." (100%, one by one)
"___ of the two vaccines showed strong results in the trial."
"___ treatment is effective for this condition — the patient will need surgery." (not one, not the other)
exercises.hint: "Neither" = not one and not the other (of two)

opts: Each of the patients were given a different dose.
Each of the patients was given a different dose.
Each of the patients are given a different dose.
Each of the patients being given a different dose.
exercises.correct: Each of the patients was given a different dose.
exercises.hint: "Each of" + singular verb in formal English

exercises.text: "___ the doctors on the team are specialists — there are no general practitioners." (100% of the group)
"You can choose ___ option — they are equally effective." (one or the other)
"___ the studies concluded the same thing: exercise reduces depression." (specific set of studies)
exercises.hint: "All of + the" refers to a specific group

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct sentence about two things.
opts: Both of the clinic is busy.

exercises.text: "She worked ___ night without sleeping." (= throughout the night)
"Neither of the options are suitable for a patient with hypertension." (formal written English)
exercises.hint: Strictly: "neither of + the + noun" → singular verb in formal English

exercises.instruction: Complete with neither, either, or both.
exercises.text: "___ diet and exercise are important for managing diabetes. Focusing on only one or the other is not enough."
exercises.hint: "Both... and" = two things together, both equally needed

exercises.text: "___ single patient matters — no one should be left without care."
exercises.hint: "Every single" = all, with emphasis on each one

exercises.text: "She didn't respond to ___ of the treatments offered." (= not one or the other)
exercises.hint: "Not... either" = negative; "neither" without "not" is also possible

exercises.instruction: Choose the sentence without an error.
opts: All of us needs more rest.
Each of the reports was reviewed carefully.
Neither of the doctors are available.
exercises.correct: Each of the reports was reviewed carefully.
exercises.hint: "Each of + the + noun + singular verb" — correct

exercises.text: "___ country was affected by the outbreak." (= the complete country, every part)
exercises.hint: "The whole + singular noun" = the complete, unbroken unit

exercises.text: "She checked ___ recommendation in the report individually before signing off."
exercises.hint: "Each" = individually, one by one (in sequence, often implies careful attention)

questions.text: "___ day brings new evidence about the benefits of exercise." (100%, singular, one by one)
"___ the participants in the study completed the questionnaire." (100% as a group)
questions.hint: "All" + plural noun = 100% as a group (or "All of")

questions.text: "___ treatment is effective for everyone — individual responses vary."
questions.hint: "No + noun" = zero instances; also "Neither" works for two options

questions.text: "___ of the two hospitals were well-equipped." (two hospitals, both)
"___ of the two treatments showed any improvement." (not one, not the other)
questions.hint: "Neither of" = not one and not the other (of two)

questions.text: "Every patients need support" is grammatically correct.
"___ of the three approaches has advantages — choose the one that suits your lifestyle."
"You can use ___ approach — both are clinically valid." (one or the other)
questions.hint: "Either" = one or the other (positive choice between two)

questions.text: "___ single system in the body is affected by poor sleep — immune, cardiac, metabolic, and cognitive." (strong emphasis, 100%)
"___ the doctor and the patient agreed on the treatment plan."
questions.hint: "Both the doctor and the patient" = two people, 100%

questions.text: "She slept ___ night — she was completely exhausted." (= the complete, unbroken night)
questions.hint: "The whole night" = the complete, uninterrupted night

opts: Both of us is committed to improving our health.
Both of us are committed to improving our health.
Both of us was committed to improving our health.
Both of us were committed to improving our health. (same as option 4)
questions.correct: Both of us are committed to improving our health.
